question: A scientist is trying to determine the proportion of white-eyed fruit flies in the environment. The white-eyed allele was found to be dominant to the red-eyed allele. The frequency of the red-eyed allele is 0.1. What is the proportion of flies who have white-eyes if the population is in Hardy Weinberg Equilibrium?
analysis: In Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium, the frequency of the dominant allele (white-eyed in this case) can be calculated using the formula p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1, where p is the frequency of the dominant allele and q is the frequency of the recessive allele. Given that the frequency of the red-eyed allele (q) is 0.1, we can calculate the frequency of the white-eyed allele (p) as 1 - 0.1 = 0.9. Therefore, the proportion of flies with white-eyes (p^2) would be 0.9^2 = 0.81, which is 81%.
